children: Gold futures settle modestly higher as U.S. yields and the dollar cede some ground. Dollar strength, rising U.S. interest-rate expectations and fading safe-haven demand have combined to undermine gold, Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com says in a note. November through January is historically a relatively strong period for gold amid year-end portfolio adjustments, renewed investment demand and seasonal jewellery purchases, he says. While that doesn't guarantee a recovery, as broader macroeconomic forces can easily override it, a strong seasonal period after such a substantial correction is a reason not to rule one out, he adds. Front month gold settles up 0.3% in New York at $3,858.80 a troy ounce. Silver rises 1.1% to $47.288 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
